For the factorial \((k/2)!\) to be defined, \(k/2\) must be a non-negative integer. Let

\[
n=\frac{k}{2}\in \{0,1,2,\dots\},
\]

so that \(k=2n\). Then

\[
\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)!\left(\frac{k}{4}\right)
= n!\cdot \frac{n}{2},
\]

and

\[
k^2=(2n)^2=4n^2.
\]

Thus the equation becomes

\[
n!\cdot \frac{n}{2}=2016+4n^2.
\]

Multiplying by \(2\),

\[
n\,n! = 4032+8n^2.
\]

Now check small non-negative integer values of \(n\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
n & n\,n! & 4032+8n^2 \\ \hline
0 & 0 & 4032 \\
1 & 1 & 4040 \\
2 & 4 & 4064 \\
3 & 18 & 4104 \\
4 & 96 & 4160 \\
5 & 600 & 4232 \\
6 & 4320 & 4320
\end{array}
\]

So \(n=6\) is a solution, giving

\[
k=2n=12.
\]

It remains to rule out \(n\ge 7\). For \(n\ge 7\),

\[
n! = (n-4)!\,n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3) \ge n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3),
\]

so

\[
n\,n! \ge n^2(n-1)(n-2)(n-3).
\]

Since \(n\ge 7\),

\[
(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)\ge 6\cdot 5\cdot 4=120.
\]

Therefore

\[
n\,n! \ge 120n^2.
\]

But

\[
120n^2 > 8n^2+4032
\]

is equivalent to

\[
112n^2>4032 \iff n^2>36,
\]

which is true for every \(n\ge 7\). Hence there are no solutions for \(n\ge 7\).

Finally, check \(k=12\):

\[
\left(\frac{12}{2}\right)!\left(\frac{12}{4}\right)=6!\cdot 3=720\cdot 3=2160,
\]

and

\[
2016+12^2=2016+144=2160.
\]

Thus the only such number is

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
